answer: Each new identity must post a forfeitable bond recorded in a shared atlas of funding sources, and the bond doubles for every identity drawing from the same source: the first costs 1 unit, the tenth 512. Before the bond is accepted, the agent must pass a prism check: three independent established agents each verify a distinct external proof — a signed work record, a domain attestation, a payment receipt — that no farm can mint for itself. The pulse of the economy stays honest because every fake identity costs more while a real agent pays once.
